value.title: ESP32 knob bridge (M5StickC firmware)
value.complexity_breakdown: S=2 (new firmware subproject, many files), I=2 (BLE HID knob + BluOS HTTP + Wi-Fi), D=1 (NVS config), N=2 (BLE HID host on ESP32 unproven here), F=2 (amp safety), T=1 (host tests + hardware smoke) = 10
value.summary: Replace the Mac-hosted Python daemon with firmware on the USB-connected M5 ESP32-PICO-D4: BLE HID host for the Anticater knob, BluOS control over Wi-Fi with the same safety caps, and a useful on-device screen.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Vaughan wants the knob-to-amp bridge to run on a cheap M5 ESP32 with a small screen instead of his Mac (thread tmwk885d1c). The firmware reimplements the daemon's small core (usage decoder, action table, increase-only max-dB refusal, safe source volume) in host-testable C++, adds a BLE HID host adapter for the knob, a Wi-Fi BluOS HTTP adapter, and a screen that shows volume, source, link state, the safety cap, and plain-language faults. It ships dry-run by default; live amp control is an explicit, visible setting, and the Mac daemon is the documented rollback.

sections.name: goals
value: Knob turns, presses and long-presses control the NAD M33 from the ESP32 with no Mac involved.
The screen always says something useful: volume in dB, source, Wi-Fi and knob link state, the safety cap, and faults in plain words.
The same safety rules as the Mac daemon: increases refused past max dB (−24 default), source switches land at a safe volume (≤ −24, default −40), dry-run until live is explicitly enabled.
Wi-Fi credentials are set by Vaughan from his terminal (`just fw-wifi`), never committed or logged.
One-command build, test, flash and monitor via the justfile.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Battery or deep-sleep optimisation (the device is USB-powered).
Multiple knobs, multiple amps, or BluOS auto-discovery (fixed host IP, configurable).
Retiring the Python daemon: it stays as the documented rollback.

value.claim: `just fw-build` compiles the firmware and `just fw-test` runs the host-native C++ tests green, with no hardware attached.
value.receipt: just fw-build SUCCESS (RAM 12.9%, Flash 61%); just fw-test 5/5

value.claim: The firmware decoder maps every real capture pattern (`03e900` up, `03ea00` down, `03e200` mute, `036f00` brightness-up, `037000` brightness-down, `030000` release) and the report-id-less BLE form (`e900`, `ea00`, …) to the same actions as `normalizer.py`.
value.receipt: firmware/test/test_decoder: report-id-3 capture vectors, report-id-less BLE form, release, unknown: 5/5 pass

value.claim: With the knob bonded to the ESP32, each gesture shows on the screen and as an action line on the serial log, and the device reconnects on its own after the knob sleeps or power-cycles.
value.receipt: Phase 1 log: all gestures on screen+serial, 0 dropped; auto-reconnect after ESP32 reset (17:29:45), fresh pairing (17:30:30), out-of-range (17:31:16→17:31:21)

value.claim: `just fw-wifi` prompts for SSID and a hidden password in the terminal, stores them in device NVS over serial, and neither value appears in serial output, logs, or git.
value.receipt: just fw-wifi: getpass prompt → NVS; show masks ****; nothing secret in git (agent-secrets check-staged clean)

value.claim: On Wi-Fi the screen shows the amp's current volume (dB) and source from BluOS; when the amp or knob is unreachable it shows a plain-language fault (e.g. "can't reach amp 192.168.1.67", "knob not connected").
value.receipt: Screen shows amp dB + source from /Volume,/Status; plain faults for Wi-Fi not found, amp unreachable, knob not connected (phase-2 log)

value.claim: A volume increase that would exceed max dB is refused and flagged on screen; source switches set volume to the safe level ≤ −24 dB; both are covered by host tests mirroring `assert_safe_step` and `safe_abs_db_value`.
value.receipt: Live refusal at cap (19:41:50, 0 writes); policy tests incl. muted-at-cap; source switch never raises (tests; live switch Deferred)

value.claim: The device ships in dry-run (shows DRY-RUN, sends no write commands). Live control is enabled only by an explicit serial command with a confirmation phrase, is remembered across restarts until `live off` (owner decision 2026-11-17), and the current mode is always shown on screen.
value.receipt: Fresh boot DRY-RUN; live only via phrase (wrong phrase refused); remembered across reboot per owner decision; badge shown

value.claim: `docs/how/esp32-bridge.md` covers flash, pairing, Wi-Fi setup, going live, and cut-over/rollback with the Mac daemon; README links it.
The screen dims after inactivity and wakes on the next knob event or status change.
value.receipt: Dimmer 30 s, wakes on knob event and volume/source change; test_timing + Vaughan confirmation

value.title: Knob to screen over BLE
value.objective: Prove and build the BLE HID host so every knob gesture shows on the device screen, with the core decoder ported and tested.
value.brief: Spike BLE first, then scaffold firmware/, TDD the decoder, build the BLE adapter and a first screen. No Wi-Fi, no amp.
delivers: Screen v1: link state + last action
value.key_risks: BLE bonding/notifications may not work with NimBLE (spike decides); smoke test takes the knob away from the Mac daemon temporarily.

value.title: Wi-Fi and read-only BluOS status
value.objective: Get the device on Wi-Fi via a terminal provisioning command and show live amp volume/source and plain-language faults, read-only.
value.brief: Config validation + NVS store + serial console, `just fw-wifi`, BluOS XML parsing from recorded fixtures, read-only polling, idle screen with dim.
delivers: Screen v2: dB, source, icons, faults, dim/wake
value.key_risks: Heap pressure with BLE + Wi-Fi together; credentials leaking into logs.

value.title: Guarded amp control and cut-over
value.objective: Port the safety policy and write commands, add the explicit live switch, and cut over from the Mac daemon with a tested rollback.
value.brief: TDD policy (refusals, safe source dB, dry-run no-writes), executor, on-turn screens, live switch, runbook, then a supervised cut-over.
delivers: Screen v3: dB + cap bar, cap flash, confirmations, DRY-RUN/LIVE
value.key_risks: Any write-path bug changes real amp volume: dry-run default, tests first, Vaughan's go-ahead before going live.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: 📚 Incorporates findings from assets/research-dossier.md: the knob is a BLE HID keyboard (`ANTICATER_MINI`, F-01) sending report-id 3 + 16-bit consumer usage (F-02); the Python daemon's decoder/policy are small and portable (F-03..F-06); the board is an ESP32-PICO-D4 M5StickC-class device (F-08); the Mac daemon is live under launchd (F-07).

value.approach: Hybrid: TDD for the portable core (decoder, command mapping, safety policy, BluOS XML field extraction, config validation) as PlatformIO native tests; manual hardware smoke checks for BLE, Wi-Fi, display and live amp control.
value.rationale: Constitution I/II and rules.md: safety clamps and normalization are TDD-worthy and must run without hardware; radio and display behaviour can only be proven on the device.
value.focus_areas: Usage decoding incl. release and report-id-less payloads; increase-only max-dB refusal; safe source dB ≤ −24; dry-run vs live gating; config validation; XML parsing of /Volume and /Status.
value.excluded: Unit tests of NimBLE, M5Unified, WiFi or HTTPClient internals.
value.mock_usage: Fakes only (constitution Testing Doubles): fake BluOS transport returning recorded XML; fake clock for dim/reconnect timers. No expectation-scripted mocks. Durable tests carry Test Doc blocks (rules.md § Test Documentation Format).

value.location: New `docs/how/esp32-bridge.md` (runbook) + a README section "Run it on an ESP32" + justfile recipe help text.
value.rationale: rules.md requires docs to change with daemon operation and config; Vaughan needs a repeatable flash/pair/rollback path.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: Assumes the board is an M5StickC or StickC Plus (ESP32-PICO-D4 with a screen); M5Unified auto-detects it. Assumes the knob accepts a bond from the ESP32 after being removed from the Mac. Assumes the amp stays at 192.168.1.67:11000 (configurable). Hardware smoke steps temporarily take the knob away from the Mac daemon and need Vaughan's go-ahead at that moment.

value.question: Exact M5 model (StickC 80×160 vs StickC Plus 135×240)?
value.note: Resolved at first boot via M5Unified board detection; layout scales to both.

value.question: Does the Mac daemon stay installed as a standby fallback after cut-over?
value.note: Default: unloaded but kept; runbook documents re-enabling it.

value.topic: BLE HID host feasibility with the Anticater knob
value.why: Novelty=2: bonding and Report notifications are unproven on this board.
value.key_questions: Does NimBLE-Arduino bond and receive 0x2A4D notifications? Payload form? Reconnect behaviour?

value.question: Workflow mode / testing / mocks / docs (Round 1)
value.answer: Decided by the bluos-knob prime under Vaughan's direction "just go ahead and build it, can always adjust afterwards" (tmwk885d1c 05:11:55Z): Full mode; Hybrid testing; fakes only per constitution; docs in docs/how + README.

value.question: Screen content
value.answer: Vaughan approved the proposed screens: idle dB/source/link icons, big dB + cap bar on turn, cap-blocked flash, mute/source confirmations, plain-language faults, dim after inactivity ("yep, those look good").

value.question: How are Wi-Fi credentials entered?
value.answer: Vaughan: "i can do it via some CLI you can help me with" → `just fw-wifi` with a hidden terminal prompt writing to NVS over serial.

value.question: Live mode: session-only (needs a computer after every restart), a 3 s button hold per power-up, or remembered across restarts?
value.answer: Vaughan (thread tmwk885d1c, 08:23:19Z): "2: remember LIVE". Live is enabled once by the serial phrase and persisted in NVS; `live off` is persisted too. Supersedes plan-review fix 3 (session-only live) by explicit owner decision; all other safety rules unchanged.

value.effect: Key findings, risks R-1..R-5, stack choice
BLE feasibility handled as Phase 1 spike instead of a workshop

value.notes: Round 1 decided under Vaughan's go-ahead; screen + Wi-Fi answered by him.
Safety-first (dry-run, caps), deterministic core, adapters, fakes, config not constants, no secrets in git, CS not time; CS-5 → staged rollout (dry-run → live) + rollback (Mac daemon).
Core policy isolated from BLE/HTTP/display; config validated before hardware use (architecture.md:70).
All sections present; phase task files linked.
Core test tasks precede implementation in each phase; hardware smoke per phase.

sections.name: implementation_summary
sections.value: A new `firmware/` PlatformIO project (espressif32, Arduino framework, M5Unified, NimBLE-Arduino). Portable logic lives in `firmware/lib/knob_core/` with no Arduino includes and is tested natively (`pio test -e native`); hardware adapters (BLE knob, Wi-Fi/BluOS HTTP, display, NVS config, serial console) sit around it in `firmware/src/`. BLE callbacks only enqueue events (H-01); one app task runs policy and HTTP. Phase 1 proves BLE and shows the knob on screen; Phase 2 adds Wi-Fi, provisioning and read-only status; Phase 3 adds guarded control, the live switch, and the cut-over runbook. Toolchain runs via `uvx` (no global installs).

value.finding: BLE HID host on ESP32 is unproven for this knob (dossier R-1).
value.action: Phase 1 starts with a throwaway spike (t1-1); go/no-go before the real adapter.

value.finding: The Mac daemon is live under launchd (F-07); two bridges could double-step the amp.
value.action: Firmware stays dry-run until cut-over; runbook unloads the plist first; live enable is explicit.

value.finding: Safety rules are increase-only max-dB refusal + safe source dB ≤ −24 (F-05, F-06).
value.action: Port into knob_core with TDD before any write path exists.

value.finding: Reports are report-id 3 + LE usage; BLE payloads likely drop the id (F-02).
value.action: Decoder scans 16-bit pairs like normalizer.py; tests cover both forms.

value.finding: PlatformIO is not installed; esptool is (F-08).
value.action: justfile recipes run `uvx --from platformio pio …`; no global install.

value.risk: NimBLE cannot bond or subscribe to the knob's reports
value.mitigation: Spike first; fallback to ESP-IDF esp_hidh under arduino-esp32 3.x.

value.risk: RAM pressure from BLE + Wi-Fi + display on PICO-D4
value.mitigation: NimBLE (smaller than Bluedroid); log free heap at boot and on screen debug page.
Dry-run default, explicit live switch, max-dB refusal tested, Vaughan's go-ahead before first live run.

value.risk: Knob stuck bonded to one host after testing
value.mitigation: Runbook: clear bonds via serial command; re-pair steps for both Mac and ESP32.
